lower_bound.quote: Insert $c$ at its first such occurrence. Until the next occurrence nothing changes; at that next occurrence the element selected there is dispensable, because that selected set is already met by $c$. Repeating between consecutive occurrences shows that the branch has a contracted node, contrary to the pruning rule.
lower_bound.witness: NON-SEQUITUR: The established premise is that one fixed $c\in C$ belongs to infinitely many sets selected along the original branch. But inserting $c$ at the first occurrence changes that branch, with no proof that subsequent nodes or selected sets remain the same. Indeed, once $c$ is inserted, every subsequently selected $F_D$ must be disjoint from the current label and therefore cannot contain $c$, so the asserted next occurrence cannot occur on the modified branch. Thus finiteness of the pruned tree does not follow.
lower_bound.load_bearing: This is the sole argument that there are finitely many minimal transversals. Without it, the finite sets $B_1,\ldots,B_s$ and hence the finite-prime description of membership have not been proved.

parsed.notes: The characterization and the global period assembly are fully written. The finite-transversal statement may be true, but its supplied search-tree proof contains the identified gap, so the required finiteness mechanism is not established by this write-up.
